agent_notes: Для פְּנֵיכֶם רָעִים в драматическом слое выбрано «лица так мрачны», тогда как Синодальный перевод говорит «печальные лица»; в буквальном слое — «лица ваши злы».

notes.note: All 23 verses are covered by an event. The framing 'after these things' (40:1) is not tied to Gen 38; chapter order is kept with the prison span of Gen 39.

[event:evt.gen_40.officers_offend] Interval after Joseph entered prison is unknown; 6 months ± 6 months is a guess. The corpus has Gen 39's prison stay ending about 1889 BCE; the chain here (custody 12 months, two dreams, feast) may run past that span's end, which is also an estimate.
[event:evt.gen_40.birthday_feast] 'Third day' counted inclusively from the interpretation day (offset 2 days); exclusive counting would give 3 days, only partly within the 12-hour margin.

[causal:caus.gen_40.butler_dream_interpreted.butler_forgets_joseph] Weak link (0.5): Joseph's request, then the cupbearer's failure. The remembrance itself is expected in Gen 41:9–13, where that chapter's session should link it.
[event:evt.gen_40.butler_forgets_joseph] Duration 2 years comes from 41:1, outside this chapter; verify against how GEN.41 anchors its first event.

[entity:person.potiphar] Identity inferred: 40:3–4 name only 'the captain of the guard' (sar ha-tabbachim), the title given to Potiphar in 37:36 and 39:1. Not stated outright in this chapter; the prison keeper of ch. 39 is a different figure.
[entity:person.chief_cupbearer] Unnamed officer; the registry has no entry. Same office as 'butler' in KJV. Kept as an entity because the plot turns on him.
[entity:person.chief_baker] Unnamed officer with no registry entry.

[entity:person.potiphar] Identity inferred: 40:3–4 name only 'the captain of the guard' (sar ha-tabbachim), the title given to Potiphar in 37:36 and 39:1. Not stated outright in this chapter; the prison keeper of ch. 39 is a different figure.
[event_links:evt.gen_40.officers_offend] No place: the offence and Pharaoh's anger are at court, which the text does not name. Left without a place rather than loc.egypt, which is a region.
[event_links:evt.gen_40.birthday_feast] No place: the feast is at Pharaoh's court, not named in the text.
[event_links:evt.gen_40.butler_restored] No place, same as the feast.
[event_links:evt.gen_40.baker_hanged] No place, same as the feast.
[event_links:evt.gen_40.butler_forgets_joseph] No place and no stated time beyond the restoration; left without place.
[event_links:evt.gen_40.officers_in_custody] The 'house of the captain of the guard' and 'the prison' are treated as one site, loc.royal_prison (as in ch. 39), since 40:3 equates them.
[component:comp.chief_cupbearer.mood.1] Expiry at 40:13 is inferred: the text does not say his mood lifts, only that he hears good news.
[component:comp.chief_baker.mood.1] Ends with his death, an inference.
[component:comp.pharaoh.mood.1] Expiry at 40:20 is inferred: the text does not say his anger ends, only that he restores one officer and hangs the other.
[component:comp.joseph.assignment.1] Joseph's open office comp.joseph.office.2 (PRISON_ADMINISTRATOR, 39:22) is left running; this is a narrower charge to attend these two.

[instance:inst.gen_40.cupbearer_vine_dream] Reuses sys.symbolic_dream for the dream plus its interpretation, with Joseph as initiator because the oracle act is the interpretation. The dreaming itself is in evt.gen_40.two_dreams without an instance.
[system:sys.royal_birthday_feast] Defined here, not reused: no existing system fits a royal birthday banquet.
[system:sys.execution_by_hanging] Defined here, not reused. The text does not say whether the baker was hanged alive or after death; both are attested.
